producer: Revision/theory/wolfram/verify_scope.wls (WolframScript, exact; no shared code with the sympy checker or with RevisionFieldTheory.wl)
spec: Revision/SPEC.md sections 1-6: scope of the non-triviality, quantisation and energy statements
coordinates: x1, x2, x3 = 3-space; x4 = time; x5, x6, x7 = the exponentially deflating extra times; x8 = the hidden direction, z = 6 H x8 in (0, Pi/2)

checks.name: fixture_gammas
checks.detail: gammas.json: {gamma^a, gamma^b} = 2 eta^ab I16 (eta = diag(1,1,1,-1,-1,-1,-1,1), order x1..x8), C = gamma^(x8) gamma^(x1) gamma^(x2) gamma^(x3), B = -i C gamma^(x4)

checks.name: boosted_frame_reproduces_metric
checks.detail: frame boosted in the (x4, x8) plane with rapidity b = beta x4 + b0: e'^(x4) = Cosh[b] e^(x4) + Sinh[b] e^(x8), e'^(x8) = Sinh[b] e^(x4) + Cosh[b] e^(x8), the other e'^(a) = e^(a) of the diagonal vielbein; e'^T eta e' equals the author's metric for all 64 entries

checks.name: boosted_frame_canonical_connection
checks.detail: canonical spin connection of the boosted frame (Christoffel symbols computed here from the author's metric): the vielbein postulate d_mu e'^a_nu - Gamma^lam_mu,nu e'^a_lam + omega_mu^a_b e'^b_nu = 0 holds for all 512 components (0 failures), omega_mu ab antisymmetric

checks.name: boosted_frame_gammaOmega_formula
checks.detail: gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = ((6 H - beta)/2) (Cosh[b] gamma^(x8) - Sinh[b] gamma^(x4)) exactly for symbolic a4[x4], H, beta, b0; control: the same code for the unboosted (diagonal) frame gives 3 H gamma^(x8)

checks.name: boosted_frame_gammaOmega_vanishes
checks.detail: rapidity b = 6 H x4 + b0: gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = 0 identically for every H > 0 and every a4[x4] (exact), in the author's curved metric; the value 3 H gamma^(x8) is a property of the diagonal vielbein, not of the field equation. Omega'_mu is nonzero for mu = x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7 and zero for x8

checks.name: boosted_frame_curvature_nonzero
checks.detail: in the boosted frame (b = 6 H x4 + b0) the spinor curvature F'_x1x8 = d_x1 Omega'_x8 - d_x8 Omega'_x1 + [Omega'_x1, Omega'_x8] is nonzero: Omega' does not vanish; no frame can make Omega vanish, because its curvature is (1/2) R_ab,mu,nu S^ab and the metric is curved

checks.name: rescaling_removes_the_connection_term
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = 3 H gamma^(x8); for Psi = Sin[z]^(-1/2) chi with 16 arbitrary functions chi_A(x1, ..., x8), gamma^mu D_mu Psi - Sin[z]^(-1/2) gamma^mu d_mu chi = 0 component by component (computed on the functions themselves): in the variables chi the field equation has no spin-connection term

checks.name: rescaled_equation_quadratic_potential
checks.detail: U = (lambda/2) S^2: S[Sin[z]^(-1/2) chi] = Sin[z]^(-1) S[chi] (the factor is real), so U'(S) Psi = Sin[z]^(-1/2) (lambda S[chi]/Sin[z]) chi and the rescaled equation is gamma^mu d_mu chi = (m + lambda S[chi]/Sin[z]) chi: the 3 H term is removed completely for U = 0 and becomes an x8-dependent coupling for U != 0

checks.name: gammaOmega_blind_to_the_deflation
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = 3 H gamma^(x8) does not contain a4 (nor a4', a4''), while R^x4_x4 = 6*Derivative[1][a4][x4]^2, R^x1_x1 = -6*H^2 + Derivative[2][a4][x4], R^x8_x8 = -6*H^2 (Riemann computed here from the metric): the deflation of the extra times is curvature that the term gamma^mu Omega_mu does not see; it enters the field equation through the frame factors E^(-+a4) Sin[z]^(-1/6)

checks.name: connection_free_lagrangian_same_equations
checks.detail: diagonal frame: {gamma^mu, Omega_mu} = 0 for each mu, so the canonical spin connection drops out of the symmetrised Lagrangian (L(Omega) = L(Omega = 0)) and the Euler-Lagrange equations are those of the connection-free symmetric Lagrangian; (1/(2 sqrt|g|)) d_mu(sqrt|g| gamma^mu) = gamma^mu Omega_mu = 3 H gamma^(x8): the half-density term

checks.name: spin_connection_in_the_energy_momentum_tensor
checks.detail: homogeneous configuration Phi(x4), diagonal frame: the connection part of K^x4_x1 = (1/2)(Phibar gamma^x4 D_x1 Phi - D_x1 Phibar gamma^x4 Phi) is (1/2) Phibar {gamma^x4, Omega_x1} Phi = (1/2) E^a4 Sin[z]^(1/6) H Phibar gamma^(x4) gamma^(x1) gamma^(x8) Phi, not identically zero: the canonical spin connection reaches the energy-momentum tensor

checks.name: good_sector_hermiticity_up_to_the_brane_flux
checks.detail: curved good-sector mode operator at k = 0, h = -i m gamma^(x4) + i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x8) (Tan[z] d_x8 + 3 H): for arbitrary complex u(x8), v(x8) (32 real functions) Cos[z] (u^dagger h v - (h u)^dagger v) = d_x8 (Sin[z] u^dagger M8 v), M8 = i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x8), exactly; the boundary term vanishes at the tip but not at z = Pi/2 (Sin[z] = 1): for gamma^(x4) gamma^(x8) u = u, u^dagger M8 u = 2*I (|u|^2 = 2). Symmetry of h for Integrate[Cos[z] u^dagger v] holds only with boundary conditions at the patch end

checks.name: good_sector_x8_independent_modes_without_boundary_condition
checks.detail: on x8-independent good-sector functions (finite norm: Integrate[Cos[6 H x8], {x8, 0, Pi/(12 H)}] = 1/(6*H)) the curved mode operator is the matrix A = -i m gamma^(x4) + 3 i H gamma^(x4) gamma^(x8): not Hermitian, A^2 = (m^2 - 9 H^2) I16; at m = H = 1 its eigenvalues are -2 Sqrt[2] i and 2 Sqrt[2] i, 8 each (modes growing like E^(2 Sqrt[2] x4)): without a boundary condition at z = Pi/2 the good sector contains complex frequencies whenever m^2 < 9 H^2

checks.name: extra_time_growth_rates_unbounded
checks.detail: flat 4+4 space (or frozen coefficients): h_k = -i m gamma^(x4) - gamma^(x4) Sum[k_a gamma^(a)] has h_k^2 = (k1^2 + k2^2 + k3^2 - k5^2 - k6^2 - k7^2 + k8^2 + m^2) I16; with k5 = K5 the growth rate Sqrt[-k1^2 - k2^2 - k3^2 + K5^2 - k8^2 - m^2] is unbounded as K5 -> Infinity: the Cauchy problem for data depending on x5, x6, x7 is not well posed in Hadamard's sense, although the slices x4 = const are non-characteristic

checks.name: commuting_field_energy_unbounded_below
checks.detail: dirac16complex00, flat frame, good sector, U = 0, m = 2, (k1, k2, k3, k8) = (1, 2, 0, 4), E = 5: [B, h_k] = 0; the E = 5 eigenspace has dimension 8 and the form u^dagger B u on it has inertia {4, 4}; the positive-frequency solutions Phi = c u E^(i (k.x - 5 x4)) (field equation verified) with B u = -u and B u = +u, |u| = 1, have energy density rho = -T^x4_x4 = -5*cc^2 and 5*cc^2 and charge density Phi^dagger B Phi = -cc^2 and cc^2 (cc = |c|): the classical energy is unbounded below already for U = 0, and the conserved charge is indefinite
